{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Full module required for all commands below except opening the host window.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. Start can replace stopped state; Resume can release an eligible retained in-dungeon run. nextstop and ns retain the save and keep Mini open until return is observed; repeat to confirm the same request. Use the existing boss-break button to cancel.

If DailyDuty is installed, /dd is unavailable for Deep Ducking; use /deepducking. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"CanUnloadAsync":false,"LoadPriority":0,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"IsHide":false,"_SourceId":"dexcss-dalamudplugins","_SourceName":"dexcss / DalamudPlugins","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json"}

{"Author":"GitHixy","Name":"LootView","Punchline":"See every item you and your party pick up, as it drops.","Description":"LootView is a live loot tracker for you and your party, with a permanent history and statistics behind it.

WHAT YOU GET

Works with every game language: English, Japanese, German and French.

- Live overlay listing every drop with its icon, rarity, quantity, who received it and how long ago.
- Estimated market value of your haul, priced for your home world through Universalis.
- Currency drawer beside the overlay with every currency you hold, its cap and the weekly tomestone limit.
- A banner on screen when another player commends you.
- Need/Greed panel that appears while rolls are open: time left on every item, each Need, Greed and Pass, who is still deciding, and the winner. Roll Need, Greed or Pass right from the panel, with the game's own loot window kept out of the way.
- Collectibles you already have (minions, mounts, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards, emotes, hairstyles, portrait frames) are marked on their icon.
- Detailed item tooltips with item level, jobs, stats, bonuses, materia slots and market price.
- Loot tables for dungeons, trials and raids - the duty you are in, or any duty you search for.
- Searchable history you can filter by item name, rarity, zone, high quality and owner.
- Statistics: rarity breakdown, top zones, daily and hourly activity, play streaks and period-over-period comparisons.
- Duty tracker recording your runs, clear times, items per run and personal bests.
- Export to JSON or CSV whenever you want.

GETTING STARTED

Type /lv to open the tracker and /lv config for settings. You can also open it from the server info bar.
Right-click any item to try it on, look it up, copy its name or blacklist it.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PRIVACY

Your history is stored locally in your Dalamud configuration folder and is never uploaded. Market prices are looked up from universalis.app and loot tables from garlandtools.org; both requests send only an item or duty ID. {"Author":"SalvatoreDevelopment","Name":"AetherFM","Punchline":"Listen to radio in Eorzea!","Description":"In-game radio streaming for Final Fantasy XIV. Enter a stream URL and listen to your favorite radio! Features external plugin integration for Umbra widgets and other plugins via reflection.

Note: AetherFM is only supported on Windows. Due to its reliance on the NAudio library, audio playback is not available on Linux or non-Windows versions of Dalamud.","Changelog":"This is a pretty big update. The directory now includes community events, Party Finder venue ads, notifications, and quite a few changes to how venues are displayed and filtered.

- Added a new Events tab. It shows FFXIV community events posted on Partake for the next two weeks, with filters for time, age rating, tags and location. You can also mark events with "I'm going" if you plan to attend.
- Party Finder venue ads collected by xivpf.com can now appear alongside events, as well as directly on the matching venue's page.
- Venues don't necessarily have to be listed on FFXIV Venues anymore. If a venue has an event on Partake or is currently advertising in Party Finder, it can still appear in the directory.
- Venue pages now show their upcoming events and any Party Finder ads that are currently active.
- Added optional notifications for favorite venues and events. The plugin can notify you when a favorite venue opens, when an event at a favorite venue starts, or 15 minutes before an event you've marked as going to. These notifications still work while the directory window is closed.
- Added "My data center" filtering. It follows the data center your current character is actually on, including after Data Center Travel. Location filters are remembered separately for each character.
- If you're standing on the plot of a listed venue, or you're already inside it, the top bar now tells you which venue you're at and gives you a quick way to mark it as visited.
- You can now hide venues you're not interested in. There's an undo option in the top bar, and hidden venues can always be found again with the Hidden filter.
- Venue descriptions now keep much more of their original formatting, including headings, bold and italic text, lists, links and images. Animated GIF, WebP and APNG images are supported too. Images in descriptions are only loaded over HTTPS and can be turned off in settings.
- Banners and images can optionally be enlarged by hovering over them. This is disabled by default.
- Locations outside the housing districts can now be opened on the in-game map.
- Settings have been moved into their own window and split into separate pages for appearance, images, events and notifications. There's also an About page with the changelog. You can use the directory's own theme or your Dalamud theme, change the UI size, and choose between a 12- or 24-hour clock.
- Schedule handling has been reworked. The directory now tries to show each venue's next actual opening in your local timezone instead of just displaying the raw weekly schedule. Monthly schedules, breaks, one-off openings and active venue notices are supported, and openings more than a week away show the date as well.
- Venue names and descriptions now show many more symbols and stylized letters; characters the game can't draw are replaced with plain letters instead of showing as boxes.
- Added a clearer error message for cases where FFXIV Venues refuses requests from your network or region.","TestingChangelog":"v1.2.0: IPC gates, Global search, Custom Stations, background playback, robustness.
- Formal IPC call gates (incl. ResumeLast, TogglePlayStop); non-throw policy; ordered events
- Global search (name/tag/language) and Custom Stations (add/list/remove)
- Favorites enhancements (names API), favorites always visible
- More stations: limit=10000, hide broken, clickcount order; wider stream validation (http/https,/stream, mp3/aac)

{"Author":"The Redheaded Witch & WillWolf76","Name":"Fashion Report Calculator / Dye Finder","Punchline":"Know your Fashion Report points on the spot and help crowdsource new items and dyes!","Description":"This is the new and improved Fashion Report System. This plugin will allow you to open a window that will show you what your fashion report status is vs the current week's theme.

There are a few parts to this. Since the only way to get Fashion Report for the week to my knowledge is speaking to Masked Rose after Tuesdays reset, this plugin takes the first person who does talk to him and updates everyone else. So only one person per week needs to speak to Masked Rose.

You can click on a theme and pull all the known items for that theme for that specific slot. You also get a very detailed breakdown of how much points you are getting based on what you are currently wearing.

The plugin also stores the attempts of those using the mod (just the data from fashioncheck, no user information) so that we can figure out the dyes faster and share information faster. The information in this table is wiped every week since once we discover the dyes, it is useless.

I still have more upgrades to do, including adding a dye window and the window that will help calculate the weekly dyes. I already have an idea of how I want to write them, so it shouldn't take me too long. If you have suggestions on how I can upgrade this, please share with me on github!

Credit for the program goes to it's original creator, WillWolf76, who wrote this for me originally.

When this plugin updates the database, it also updates my Discord Bot which you can set up to post fashion report each week. It's set to update on Tuesdays and Fridays (week start and dye information added). Link to add the Discord Bot is in the about section.","Changelog":"This is a pretty big update. The directory now includes community events, Party Finder venue ads, notifications, and quite a few changes to how venues are displayed and filtered.

- Added a new Events tab. It shows FFXIV community events posted on Partake for the next two weeks, with filters for time, age rating, tags and location. You can also mark events with "I'm going" if you plan to attend.
- Party Finder venue ads collected by xivpf.com can now appear alongside events, as well as directly on the matching venue's page.
- Venues don't necessarily have to be listed on FFXIV Venues anymore. If a venue has an event on Partake or is currently advertising in Party Finder, it can still appear in the directory.
- Venue pages now show their upcoming events and any Party Finder ads that are currently active.
- Added optional notifications for favorite venues and events. The plugin can notify you when a favorite venue opens, when an event at a favorite venue starts, or 15 minutes before an event you've marked as going to. These notifications still work while the directory window is closed.
- Added "My data center" filtering. It follows the data center your current character is actually on, including after Data Center Travel. Location filters are remembered separately for each character.
- If you're standing on the plot of a listed venue, or you're already inside it, the top bar now tells you which venue you're at and gives you a quick way to mark it as visited.
- You can now hide venues you're not interested in. There's an undo option in the top bar, and hidden venues can always be found again with the Hidden filter.
- Venue descriptions now keep much more of their original formatting, including headings, bold and italic text, lists, links and images. Animated GIF, WebP and APNG images are supported too. Images in descriptions are only loaded over HTTPS and can be turned off in settings.
- Banners and images can optionally be enlarged by hovering over them. This is disabled by default.
- Locations outside the housing districts can now be opened on the in-game map.
- Settings have been moved into their own window and split into separate pages for appearance, images, events and notifications. There's also an About page with the changelog. You can use the directory's own theme or your Dalamud theme, change the UI size, and choose between a 12- or 24-hour clock.
- Schedule handling has been reworked. The directory now tries to show each venue's next actual opening in your local timezone instead of just displaying the raw weekly schedule. Monthly schedules, breaks, one-off openings and active venue notices are supported, and openings more than a week away show the date as well.
- Venue names and descriptions now show many more symbols and stylized letters; characters the game can't draw are replaced with plain letters instead of showing as boxes.
- Added a clearer error message for cases where FFXIV Venues refuses requests from your network or region.","TestingChangelog":"Minor bug fixes including the rendering of item data on a new week, sometimes would still display the previous weeks item list instead. Disabled the judging window due to problem detecting the opening of the FashionCheck addon during judging until I can find a work around.","Tags":["Fashion Report","Gold Saucer","Mini Game","Masked Rose","Glamour","MGP"],"CategoryTags":["Utility","UI"],"IsHide":true,"InternalName":"FashionReport","AssemblyVersion":"1.2.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.2.0.0","IsTestingExclusive":true,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/TheRedheadedWitch/FashionReport","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":13,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":13,"DownloadCount":336,"LastUpdate":1764128162,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/FashionReport?isUpdate=False&isTesting=False&branch=api9&isDip17=True","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goatcorp/DalamudPlugins/api9/plugins/FashionReport/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/FashionReport?isUpdate=False&isTesting=True&branch=api9&isDip17=True","LoadPriority":0,"ImageUrls":null,"IconUrl":"https://github.com/TheRedheadedWitch/FashionReport/raw/main/FashionReport/images/icon.png","AcceptsFeedback":true,"FeedbackMessage":null,"FeedbackWebhook":null,"_isDip17Plugin":true,"_Dip17Channel":"testing-live"}

{"Author":"AEBus","Name":"FFXIV Venues Directory","Punchline":"Browse FFXIV roleplay venues in-game with rich filters and schedules.","Description":"Discover open FFXIV venues by region, data center, world, tags, and schedule. View detailed venue cards with addresses, banners, and external links directly in-game.","Changelog":"This is a pretty big update. The directory now includes community events, Party Finder venue ads, notifications, and quite a few changes to how venues are displayed and filtered.

- Added a new Events tab. It shows FFXIV community events posted on Partake for the next two weeks, with filters for time, age rating, tags and location. You can also mark events with "I'm going" if you plan to attend.
- Party Finder venue ads collected by xivpf.com can now appear alongside events, as well as directly on the matching venue's page.
- Venues don't necessarily have to be listed on FFXIV Venues anymore. If a venue has an event on Partake or is currently advertising in Party Finder, it can still appear in the directory.
- Venue pages now show their upcoming events and any Party Finder ads that are currently active.
- Added optional notifications for favorite venues and events. The plugin can notify you when a favorite venue opens, when an event at a favorite venue starts, or 15 minutes before an event you've marked as going to. These notifications still work while the directory window is closed.
- Added "My data center" filtering. It follows the data center your current character is actually on, including after Data Center Travel. Location filters are remembered separately for each character.
- If you're standing on the plot of a listed venue, or you're already inside it, the top bar now tells you which venue you're at and gives you a quick way to mark it as visited.
- You can now hide venues you're not interested in. There's an undo option in the top bar, and hidden venues can always be found again with the Hidden filter.
- Venue descriptions now keep much more of their original formatting, including headings, bold and italic text, lists, links and images. Animated GIF, WebP and APNG images are supported too. Images in descriptions are only loaded over HTTPS and can be turned off in settings.
- Banners and images can optionally be enlarged by hovering over them. This is disabled by default.
- Locations outside the housing districts can now be opened on the in-game map.
- Settings have been moved into their own window and split into separate pages for appearance, images, events and notifications. There's also an About page with the changelog. You can use the directory's own theme or your Dalamud theme, change the UI size, and choose between a 12- or 24-hour clock.
- Schedule handling has been reworked. The directory now tries to show each venue's next actual opening in your local timezone instead of just displaying the raw weekly schedule. Monthly schedules, breaks, one-off openings and active venue notices are supported, and openings more than a week away show the date as well.
- Venue names and descriptions now show many more symbols and stylized letters; characters the game can't draw are replaced with plain letters instead of showing as boxes.
- Added a clearer error message for cases where FFXIV Venues refuses requests from your network or region.","TestingChangelog":"This is a pretty big update. {"Author":"Bronya Rand","Name":"Things To Do In Eorzea","Punchline":"Unsure what to do? Forgot what you wanted to do? Nonsense! There's always things to do in Eorzea!","Description":"
Keep track of all your objectives and tasks in Eorzea. Whether it's collecting tomes/items/gear, completing dungeons/trials/raids, FATEs, or purely making a random list of things to do to keep yourself busy, keep yourself organized and on track with this plugin.

Features:
    - Create and manage a list of objectives and tasks.
    - Automatically track your progress on objectives and tasks.
    - View your objectives and tasks with a window inspired by the in-game Duty Log.
    - Automatic translation of objectives and tasks to your game client's language. (No need to write what you want to do. Just setup how you want to do it and the plugin will fill in the rest!)
    - Open creativity for just about anything that comes up to mine! (...What? You don't think making silly challenges like doing Endsinger's Aria - Extreme with MINE in under 12 minutes a good idea? Seriously, you can make that a task if you want)
       
Inspired by the idea of "DYOM" (Design Your Own Mission) and "TTDISA" (Things To Do In San Andreas) from GTA: San Andreas as well as Simple To-Do List and other similar plugins.
    ","Changelog":"# LiteShade

A little less green.

Colour adjustments, GPose filters, optional depth of field and vignette.
Uses the game's own effects and leaves the UI alone.

It's one that automatically monitors what you need to collect, what duties you need to clear, FATEs and more! You can either set it up to track items you need or have it track your clears. Think that's not enough? You can even set yourself up some ridiculous tasks for yourself like doing MINE Bahamut or a whole Savage round without dying/wiping to just simply forcing yourself to play a specific job, or speedrun. There are always things to do in Eorzea. Just get creative!

Unlike other to-do plugins, Things To Do In Eorzea:
1. Auto-tracks your completed dungeons, trials and raids.
2. Auto-tracks your completed FATEs by region, a specific FATE or any FATE in general.
3. Auto-tracks the items in your inventory, making sure you have what you needed to get.
4. Make self-imposed challenges like doing Minstrel's Ballads on MINE difficulty, speedrun a Dungeon, one-shot/no kill, and more.
5. Read objectives in your native language*

   > French is partially broken ATM pending a Dalamud merge.

And you still have your sticky note for whenever you need it.

AI Use: Assist
> AI was used to inquire about translations from English to Japanese to show there was at least an attempt to show that localization is supported. However said translations may not be accurate. Anyone interested may PR or DM me their translated findings for German, Japanese and French if they so please. Thus far:
> - Full English on UI and Objective Display
> - Full Japanese [Claude+Gemini+Google Translate+DeepL+Japanese Dictionary] on UI and Objective Display
> - German only on the Objective Display with partial assistance from XIV community for macros and Claude
> - French only on the Objective DIsplay with assistance from Gemini and Clause
> 
> There was also AI assist for the localization system.","Tags":["to-do,list,track,task,objective,custom,utility,ui,other"],"CategoryTags":["utility","ui","other"],"IsHide":true,"InternalName":"ThingsToDoInEorzea","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.0.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"1.0.0.0","IsTestingExclusive":true,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/Bronya-Rand/ThingsToDoInEorzea.git","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"DownloadCount":688,"LastUpdate":1787607241,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=False&branch=api9&isDip17=True","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/goatcorp/DalamudPlugins/api9/plugins/ThingsToDoInEorzea/latest.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://kamori.goats.dev/Plugin/Download/ThingsToDoInEorzea?isUpdate=False&isTesting=True&branch=api9&isDip17=True","LoadPriority":0,"ImageUrls":null,"IconUrl":null,"AcceptsFeedback":true,"FeedbackMessage":null,"FeedbackWebhook":null,"_isDip17Plugin":true,"_Dip17Channel":"testing-live"}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Armoire Auto-Fill","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.5.7.0","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".

v0.5.3.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The "Copy import code" instructions now name the exact controls.** After copying, the message says which currency window to open (the sidebar entry under "Currencies"), that the shopping-list dropdown sits at the top of the window next to "Buy All", and that the import is the clipboard icon labelled "Paste" at the right end of the "New list name..." row. It also names the list that will be created, quotes the confirmation line Knightshopper prints in chat ("Imported the shopping list from the clipboard."), and explains that each code only imports in its own currency's window - pasted elsewhere, Knightshopper refuses it and says which window to use.
- Currency names now match Knightshopper's own labels ("The Hunt" instead of "Hunt", "Tomestones" instead of "Tomestone", "Scrips" instead of "Scrip"), so the headings, the created list names and the instructions match what the sidebar shows.
- When Knightshopper is not loaded, the hint now points at the same controls instead of just saying "paste them".

v0.5.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **The shopping list now builds.** On the previous testing build the Knightshopper shopping list always showed "Shop catalog unavailable": one shop entry with an unusual data shape aborted the whole catalog. That entry is now skipped instead, the rest of the list still builds, and a failure is no longer retried every frame.
- The section now says what actually happened: game data not ready yet, a build failure (with a Refresh button — nothing retries automatically), or a normal empty result ("nothing to shop for").

- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. - Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Lazy Market Companion","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.8.15","CategoryTags":["utility"],"Changelog":"v0.2.8.16 (2026-10-17) [testing]
- **Fresh installs no longer show an import notice for a plugin that was never installed.** A leftover line in the configuration loader set the "imported from Dagobert Price Matcher" flag true on every load that created a new configuration, so a brand-new install showed the import notice and the uninstall hint even though no settings were ever imported. The flag now keeps its false default; a genuine import from a found Dagobert configuration still sets it, and the load log's imported= field reports the real value.
- Untried build: tested offline against the plugin's offline test suite, not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.15 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.
- Untried build: tested offline against a saved-configuration round trip (the plugin's offline test suite), not yet in the game.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.

- **The Auto-Market panel's two filter dropdowns remember their setting between sessions.** The status filter (every stack / on the list / not on the list / excluded) and the market-category filter used to reset to "every stack, every category" every time the plugin loaded or the game restarted; they now save as soon as they are changed and come back that way. A saved category the current bags do not contain still shows as "every category" instead of silently hiding everything, and the saved choice comes back when the bags hold that category again.

v0.2.8.14 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **A pinch row that cannot get its dialog or its price is now skipped; it no longer aborts the whole retainer with the price dialog left open.** Each row step waits for a dialog or a market price. When one never arrived, the wait ran into the task manager's hard 10-second limit, which discards every remaining task of the run and leaves the dialog on screen. Each row step now has a shorter budget of its own: when it runs out, the row is skipped with a log line naming the stage and row, the row's dialogs are closed, any late market reply is dropped, and the run carries on with the next row. A skipped row keeps its current price.
- **A Universalis timeout is no longer mistaken for a cancellation.** The sale-history lookup used when the market board is empty (and the data-center price lookup) swallowed the HTTP client's own 8-second timeout as if the run had been cancelled, so no answer was ever delivered and the row waited out the hard limit. A timeout is now reported as a failed lookup ("Universalis did not answer in time") and the row falls back to the normal no-price handling.
- **The empty-board sale-history wait now actually times out.** Its 6-second deadline could never be reached because the pending candidate price was cleared on every retry; the candidate is now kept while the lookup is pending.
- **A run that does stop (a step timeout, a session cap, a vendoring halt) closes what it left open before AutoRetainer is handed back.** The price dialog, item menu, market result, sell list and retainer inventory panel are closed innermost-first within a few seconds, the retainer menu is left for AutoRetainer, and the buyback-abandon confirm is never touched. The log names the last stage and what was closed.
- **The AutoRetainer session cap grows with the number of rows the session queued** instead of staying a flat five minutes, so a long pinch list at slow market-board delays is not cut off.
- **A manual sweep that reaches a retainer's buyback-abandon confirm now parks there with a plain report** instead of letting the next retainer's click wait out the hard limit and abort with a generic timeout. The report names the retainers that did not run.
- **An interrupted manual sweep can be resumed.** Starting the sweep again within 30 minutes runs only the retainers that had not finished; retainers that finished are not re-priced.
- Untried build: the guard was tested offline against a simulated task chain and the plugin source, not yet in the game.

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","AcceptsFeedback":true,"ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","CanUnloadAsync":false,"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Changelog":"v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. A v5 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging. v0.3.4.0: Fix the self-kan freeze. A Kan/Pass bar at state 6 is ignored and the normal discard proceeds instead of firing a Pass callback the client ignores. Session stats are preserved after /mjadv stop so the bundle still shows the run, and a v4 config migration re-enables auto-play/logging for the next launch. v0.3.3.0: Reset the exposed tuning sliders to the fitted win-rate defaults (base hand value 1300, deal-in 5200, noten 1500, opponent hand 4000) with a one-time v3 config migration. Diagnostic bundles now include the actual Dalamud plugin config file from pluginConfigs. v0.3.2.0: State 15 is now treated as the generic other-players state unless real call buttons are present, state 22 (forced riichi discard) is automated, and state 27 (between-hands result/score) is recognised instead of showing stale advice. Overlay/advice are now gated to actual decision states, and diagnostic bundles can read the Dalamud log while it is open. v0.3.1.0: Auto-play and file logging are now on by default, /mjadv session starts a clean logged session, and /mjadv bundle packages the recent JSONL logs, config, layouts, Dalamud log tail and a full last-read snapshot into one zip. Status changes are now logged as auto-status records. v0.3.0.1: Re-arm auto-play on a state change even when the hand happens to repeat, and wait for the Riichi/Pass prompt to close before cutting the riichi tile. v0.3.0.0: Optional auto-play. Replays the client's FireCallback protocol for discards, calls, riichi, ron/tsumo and result advancement, using the reference solver's live-verified handshake and timing guards. Off by default; /mjadv auto [on/off] or /mjadv stop toggles it. Pon/ron/tsumo/riichi are enabled by default, chi and kan are opt-in, the chi shape picker pauses for a manual choice, and the new-hand screen is never auto-advanced. Added /mjadv hand and /mjadv options diagnostics. v0.2.0.2: Keep the previous wall count, so the wall-jump half of new-hand detection actually fires. v0.2.0.1: Reset the pond baselines at the start of a new hand, so the first discard of the hand is tracked and the first call prompt gets the right claimed tile. v0.2.0.0: Meld containers now read by default (112-115 families), with a fail-closed check against our own called-meld count. Own meld tiles are recovered from hand deltas when nodes are unavailable, so ukeire no longer counts tiles already in a call. Riichi detection is marker-node only; the dead rotation and score-drop paths are gone. One node-tree walk per read instead of up to seven. Fixed dead hands getting a nonzero win rate and Pass inventing a yaku path. Red-five decoding accepts both absolute and alias ids. Removed the obsolete fold-threshold setting. Setup window no longer reopens every launch. Added /mjadv melds diagnostics and richer log records.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/dexcss/DalamudPlugins/main/repo.json","DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor/releases/latest/download/MahjongAdvisor.zip","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","IsTestingExclusive":false,"LoadPriority":0,"LoadRequiredState":0,"LoadSync":false,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15}

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.3 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare game version 7.57**, and their source-code metadata points to the current rotation paths.
- **Paladin Guardian uses only the configured general-ability checks.** Duplicate attack-ability triggers that could bypass the HP and Hallowed Ground settings are removed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.2 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **When BossModReborn is unloaded, its timeline data (upcoming raidwides, tankbusters, knockbacks) is cleared once**, so proactive mitigation no longer acts on countdowns left over from before the unload.
- The last plugin lookup that could log an error on every call (the BossModReborn version lookup) reads the installed-plugin list instead.
- The BossModReborn check writes one log line when it first finds (or does not find) BossModReborn and one each time it is loaded or unloaded, never one per frame.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.1 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **BossModReborn integration was never detected, and it filled the log with errors.** The check for BossModReborn (and for WrathCombo) went through a lookup that cannot read BossModReborn's plugin object, so it reported the plugin as missing even while loaded, and wrote an error with a stack trace to the Dalamud log each time it was asked, once per frame while the settings window was open (over 11,000 lines in 35 minutes). The check now reads the list of installed plugins and quietly reports whether the plugin is loaded, so the BossModReborn timeline data is used when BossModReborn is running and the log stays clean.

v0.1.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **New settings window.** `/pvpsolver`, the plugin's settings button and Lazy Hub now open a new window with the settings that matter for PvP, in plain words with a help line under each. It has six tabs: Match (when PvP Solver turns itself on and off), Survival (Guard, Purify, Sprint and the defensives master switch), Targeting (who to attack, area attacks, burst, invulnerable enemies), My Job, Display and Advanced.
- **Settings can be changed in any zone.** Every setting, including each job's own options, can be edited anywhere and for any of the 21 jobs, not only for the played job inside a PvP zone. Only turning PvP Solver on still needs a PvP zone; its button says so. Job options need a character in the world.
- **Optional automatic defensives, all off by default.** Each is a "use when HP is below" setting with its own percentage, per job, in the My Job tab: Aquaveil (White Mage), Wreath of Ice (Black Mage), Tempera Coat (Pictomancer), Forte (Red Mage), Radiant Aegis (Summoner), Arcane Crest (Reaper), Snake Scales (Viper), The Blackest Night (Dark Knight), Holy Sheltron (Paladin), Bloodwhetting (Warrior), Curing Waltz (Dancer), and the PvP role actions Rampart (tanks) and Stoneskin II (healers), which can be used only while they are the selected role action. Recuperate keeps its existing rule (15,000 or more HP missing) and gains an optional second condition, an HP percentage. Default percentages run from 45 to 70.
- **Defensives master switch.** One switch in the Survival tab (on by default) turns all automatic defensives off at once. It also covers the six that were already automatic at a fixed HP: Heart of Corundum, Riddle of Earth, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui and Impalement, so turning it off stops those too.
- **Worst case of the defensives.** After one automatic defensive is used no other is used for 2.5 seconds, and none while a barrier, damage reduction or heal of the same kind from another turned-on defensive is still active, but with several turned on, more than one can still be used during one long stretch of low HP.
- **Six fixed HP thresholds are now settings with unchanged defaults.** Heart of Corundum (Gunbreaker) at or below 30%, Riddle of Earth (Monk) below 80%, Lady of Crowns and Microcosmos (Astrologian) below 60%, Meisui (Ninja) below 50% and Impalement (Dark Knight) below 60% behave exactly as before until changed. Each can be moved or turned off in the My Job tab.
- **Job options are stored per job.** Options were stored under the job being played, and the first time a job was used in a session its options shared one store, so same-named options (the Bloodbath and Smite thresholds of the six melee jobs) could carry over from one job to another. Each job's options are now stored under that job. Saved settings are kept.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The previous settings window is still available: Advanced tab, or `/pvpsolver advanced` (optionally followed by a tab name such as Actions).
- No saved setting is renamed or lost. The new settings use new keys that appear in the settings file only after they are changed.
- Checked offline only so far: the window layout, the automatic defensives with real targets and the job options of a job that is not being played have not yet been run in a match.

v0.1.1.5 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Targeting selection in PvP.** Entering the PvP state forced lowest-HP targeting, so the configured targeting list and the focus-fire (`PvPHighestPressure`) mode could not be selected. The configured list now applies; with default settings targeting is unchanged (lowest HP first).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.1.4 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Tank ability stall in PvP.** With several enemies in melee range and a tank's own mitigation on cooldown, the rotation stopped issuing every later ability until the situation ended. The defensive stage now hands over to the rest of the rotation in PvP.
- **Melee attack abilities considered at 5 yalms.** Melee jobs considered their attack abilities only with an enemy within 3 yalms although their weaponskills reach 5; in PvP the check now uses 5 yalms. Each ability still checks its own range.
- **Smite ignores Guard.** The target filter no longer excludes an enemy that has Guard when Smite is the action.
- **Sprint and Purify with no enemy nearby.** The list of actions allowed with no enemy within 40 yalms named the wrong actions; PvP Sprint and Purify are now allowed.
- **White Mage and Bard Guard, Recuperate and Elixir on the GCD path.** The emergency GCD step ended in the wrong base step and skipped them.
- **Scholar Chain Stratagem condition** now checks the enemy the action will actually target.
- **Viper Rattling Coil** no longer waits on Snake Scales, which the rotation never uses.
- **Gunbreaker.** The Blasting Zone 50% check reads the chosen target; the Heart of Corundum self-save now targets the Gunbreaker.
- **Paladin Guardian** respects the Hallowed Ground HP threshold and the 10-yalm limit.
- **Warden's Paean on allies (Bard) and Aquaveil on allies (White Mage).** The optional cleanse of other players could never find a target because it only counted afflictions the caster had applied; it now counts any affliction. Both options remain off by default.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.

v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]

- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.310 (2026-10-17)

- NIN: fixed a Kassatsu sync issue.
- DTR bar entry: right-click now opens the UI; the auto-rotation toggle moved to left-click.
- PvP: fixed hotbar saving writing to the wrong slot.
- SAM: fixed the FRU opener.
- MCH: removed an unused target setting; job config cleanups across many jobs.

v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","Punchline":"PvP-only auto-rotation","Description":"PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.","InternalName":"PvPSolver","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.2.4","Changelog":"v0.1.2.4 (2026-10-22) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare the upstream "Reborn" rotation type** (RotationSolverReborn 79f60d87c), upstream's tag for rotations written for the pre-Evercold job kits. Metadata only; rotations load and behave as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.3 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare game version 7.57**, and their source-code metadata points to the current rotation paths.
- **Paladin Guardian uses only the configured general-ability checks.** Duplicate attack-ability triggers that could bypass the HP and Hallowed Ground settings are removed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.2 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **When BossModReborn is unloaded, its timeline data (upcoming raidwides, tankbusters, knockbacks) is cleared once**, so proactive mitigation no longer acts on countdowns left over from before the unload.
- The last plugin lookup that could log an error on every call (the BossModReborn version lookup) reads the installed-plugin list instead.
- The BossModReborn check writes one log line when it first finds (or does not find) BossModReborn and one each time it is loaded or unloaded, never one per frame.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.1 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **BossModReborn integration was never detected, and it filled the log with errors.** The check for BossModReborn (and for WrathCombo) went through a lookup that cannot read BossModReborn's plugin object, so it reported the plugin as missing even while loaded, and wrote an error with a stack trace to the Dalamud log each time it was asked, once per frame while the settings window was open (over 11,000 lines in 35 minutes). The check now reads the list of installed plugins and quietly reports whether the plugin is loaded, so the BossModReborn timeline data is used when BossModReborn is running and the log stays clean.

v0.1.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **New settings window.** `/pvpsolver`, the plugin's settings button and Lazy Hub now open a new window with the settings that matter for PvP, in plain words with a help line under each. It has six tabs: Match (when PvP Solver turns itself on and off), Survival (Guard, Purify, Sprint and the defensives master switch), Targeting (who to attack, area attacks, burst, invulnerable enemies), My Job, Display and Advanced.
- **Settings can be changed in any zone.** Every setting, including each job's own options, can be edited anywhere and for any of the 21 jobs, not only for the played job inside a PvP zone. Only turning PvP Solver on still needs a PvP zone; its button says so. Job options need a character in the world.
- **Optional automatic defensives, all off by default.** Each is a "use when HP is below" setting with its own percentage, per job, in the My Job tab: Aquaveil (White Mage), Wreath of Ice (Black Mage), Tempera Coat (Pictomancer), Forte (Red Mage), Radiant Aegis (Summoner), Arcane Crest (Reaper), Snake Scales (Viper), The Blackest Night (Dark Knight), Holy Sheltron (Paladin), Bloodwhetting (Warrior), Curing Waltz (Dancer), and the PvP role actions Rampart (tanks) and Stoneskin II (healers), which can be used only while they are the selected role action. Recuperate keeps its existing rule (15,000 or more HP missing) and gains an optional second condition, an HP percentage. Default percentages run from 45 to 70.
- **Defensives master switch.** One switch in the Survival tab (on by default) turns all automatic defensives off at once. It also covers the six that were already automatic at a fixed HP: Heart of Corundum, Riddle of Earth, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui and Impalement, so turning it off stops those too.
- **Worst case of the defensives.** After one automatic defensive is used no other is used for 2.5 seconds, and none while a barrier, damage reduction or heal of the same kind from another turned-on defensive is still active, but with several turned on, more than one can still be used during one long stretch of low HP.
- **Six fixed HP thresholds are now settings with unchanged defaults.** Heart of Corundum (Gunbreaker) at or below 30%, Riddle of Earth (Monk) below 80%, Lady of Crowns and Microcosmos (Astrologian) below 60%, Meisui (Ninja) below 50% and Impalement (Dark Knight) below 60% behave exactly as before until changed. Each can be moved or turned off in the My Job tab.
- **Job options are stored per job.** Options were stored under the job being played, and the first time a job was used in a session its options shared one store, so same-named options (the Bloodbath and Smite thresholds of the six melee jobs) could carry over from one job to another. Each job's options are now stored under that job. Saved settings are kept.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- The previous settings window is still available: Advanced tab, or `/pvpsolver advanced` (optionally followed by a tab name such as Actions).
- No saved setting is renamed or lost. The new settings use new keys that appear in the settings file only after they are changed.
- Checked offline only so far: the window layout, the automatic defensives with real targets and the job options of a job that is not being played have not yet been run in a match.

v0.1.1.5 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Targeting selection in PvP.** Entering the PvP state forced lowest-HP targeting, so the configured targeting list and the focus-fire (`PvPHighestPressure`) mode could not be selected. The configured list now applies; with default settings targeting is unchanged (lowest HP first).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.1.4 (2026-10-07) [testing]
- **Tank ability stall in PvP.** With several enemies in melee range and a tank's own mitigation on cooldown, the rotation stopped issuing every later ability until the situation ended. The defensive stage now hands over to the rest of the rotation in PvP.
- **Melee attack abilities considered at 5 yalms.** Melee jobs considered their attack abilities only with an enemy within 3 yalms although their weaponskills reach 5; in PvP the check now uses 5 yalms. Each ability still checks its own range.
- **Smite ignores Guard.** The target filter no longer excludes an enemy that has Guard when Smite is the action.
- **Sprint and Purify with no enemy nearby.** The list of actions allowed with no enemy within 40 yalms named the wrong actions; PvP Sprint and Purify are now allowed.
- **White Mage and Bard Guard, Recuperate and Elixir on the GCD path.** The emergency GCD step ended in the wrong base step and skipped them.
- **Scholar Chain Stratagem condition** now checks the enemy the action will actually target.
- **Viper Rattling Coil** no longer waits on Snake Scales, which the rotation never uses.
- **Gunbreaker.** The Blasting Zone 50% check reads the chosen target; the Heart of Corundum self-save now targets the Gunbreaker.
- **Paladin Guardian** respects the Hallowed Ground HP threshold and the 10-yalm limit.
- **Warden's Paean on allies (Bard) and Aquaveil on allies (White Mage).** The optional cleanse of other players could never find a target because it only counted afflictions the caster had applied; it now counts any affliction. Both options remain off by default.

{"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

Full module required for all commands below except opening the host window.

Commands (use /deepducking; /dduck is an alias):
/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
