- **Switches and settings for the whole suite.** Plugins that offer controls can be turned on or off and have their common settings changed from the hub, over Dalamud IPC. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the owning plugin's own window does; the hub never writes another plugin's configuration.
- **Quick tab:** a Gluttony Combo tray with the Auto-Rotation switch and hotbar buttons (click a button, then click a hotbar slot to place the action; Escape cancels), then one switch per plugin that offers one. Switches with real consequences (Auto-Market, the FATE bot) ask for a second click within a few seconds.
- **Plugin page:** the plugin's settings in groups: switches, number steppers (`-` and `+`) and option pickers (`<` and `>`). A setting that another plugin or a running task holds is shown as locked with the reason and refuses changes.
- **Plugins tab:** all fifteen plugins with status, Settings and Open. A plugin on a version that does not offer controls yet has Open only.
- **Safe mode:** `/lazy safe` switches to the plain window and back. The choice is remembered.
- **Look:** the window frame is tinted toward lalalazy green with forest-green panels, gold accents and each plugin's icon.

- **Plugin icons fit their slot.** They were drawn at their full 64-pixel size instead of the 44-pixel slot, which covered the first letters of each name and status line and touched the row below.

- Testing channel only. Plugins offer controls from the versions released with this one: update them to see their settings here.
- The hub asks each plugin for its controls about once a second while the window is open and not at all while it is closed.
- After an update the "What's new" window shows these notes once. `/lazy changelog` reopens them.

{"Author":"Akari","Name":"Mahjong Advisor","InternalName":"Mahjong.Advisor.Plugin","AssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.4.3.0","IsTestingExclusive":false,"RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dexcss/MahjongAdvisor","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"MinimumDalamudVersion":null,"Tags":["mahjong","doman","gold-saucer","auto-play","advisor"],"CategoryTags":["Utility"],"Punchline":"Discard advice and optional auto-play for Doman Mahjong.","Description":"Reads your Doman Mahjong hand, discards, dora, scores and called melds, then ranks each discard by hand speed against deal-in risk. Auto-play and file logging are on by default in this build: sit at a casual table and it plays, then /mjadv bundle packages the logs for support. /mjadv stop or the Automation tab returns to manual suggestions instantly. Discard piles and meld strips are found automatically; the node tools are only a fallback.","Changelog":"v0.4.3.0: Result-screen retry. The result panel can swallow the first advance callback while it animates; the controller fired it twice and then its acted guard blocked every retry, leaving the screen waiting indefinitely (live Advanced freeze, state 29 unresolved for 12s). Advances now retry every 2.5 seconds while the result state persists, capped at 8 attempts so the deliberately manual match-end screen is not spammed. v0.4.2.0: Match-level tuning. A full hanchan evaluator now plays East+South with real score accounting, dealer rotation, honcha, riichi sticks and placement, and 120 paired matches showed the old risk settings were too passive. Win value 1800 and deal-in cost 4000 beat 1300/5200 on identical deals (average place 2.55 vs 2.65, more firsts, fewer fourths) with the deal-in rate unchanged at 9.3%. A v7 config migration applies the new values. Riichi hand value and placement stance were also tested and left unchanged - both were flat across 60-match arms. v0.4.1.0: Advanced-table defence. Cross-seat genbutsu now uses the pond lengths captured at the instant a riichi marker appears; the old turn-count shortcut broke once calls shortened ponds and could mark a tile discarded before the riichi as safe. Two declared riichi also force a fold for any hand that is not tenpai, overriding the placement chase. The simulator now records the same declaration snapshots: over 1,000 hands the defence fix moved deal-in rate from 10.3% to 9.5% and average points from -22 to +17, while the double-riichi rail was neutral there because the simulation has no placement stance. Live Advanced trial on 0.4.0.0 finished 1st, 4th, then leading when stopped; the 4th lost two deal-ins to one riichi player, the second 12,000 while two were in riichi. v0.4.0.0: Exact scoring core. Completed hands are now scored by yaku, fu, dora and the payment table (closed and open, riichi through yakuman), and the offline simulator uses that scoring for win legality and payouts. Ready-hand valuation was built and benchmarked but stays out of live decisions: over 1,500 simulated hands, mixing exact tenpai values with the existing one-away estimate cut the win rate from 15.4% to 8.1%, so the value scale must be unified for every shanten first. Advice is memoised per table state so the overlay and controller do not recompute the same decision. v0.3.10.0: Silent-endgame defence. The threat model measured a silent opponent as at most 19% likely tenpai, so on a table with no riichi and no melds every safety rule stayed off - the controller pushed one-away hands with 6-9 tiles left to draw into damaten twice in one match (4,200 and 2,200 deal-ins) and paid full tsumo on 14,300 and 20,000 hands. Silent seats now take on a readiness floor that rises from zero at wall 32 to a concrete threat at wall 16, arming the existing late-wall fold and per-tile safety ranking on quiet tables. v0.3.9.0: Chi freeze fixed. The shape-selection dialog ignores scripted call picks (confirmed by the first picker dump), so chi now only fires when exactly one shape is possible - that path completes with no dialog. Multi-shape chi passes instead of stalling; the pass log records how many shapes were declined. v0.3.8.0: Late-wall defence. When an opponent is a concrete threat and the wall is down to the last four go-arounds, the controller folds any hand that is not tenpai instead of pushing a 1-shanten no-riichi hand. This was the 12,000 deal-in in the first match. Diagnostic bundles now also include chi picker dumps. The end-of-match results screen still waits for you by design - that is the one click after a match. v0.3.7.0: Chi is now fully automated. The controller calls chi when the advisor ranks it best, and if the client shows the shape-selection surface it fires the first variant and re-evaluates the hand. The picker layout is dumped once per session to the log folder so shape-specific selection can be refined against real captures. A v6 config migration enables chi. v0.3.6.0: Read each opponent meld strip independently. A hidden empty strip for one quiet seat no longer suppresses every visible meld on the table, so the threat model sees called sets when they exist. This is a readiness/defence accuracy change; automation logic is unchanged. v0.3.5.0: Fix the second freeze. A complete open hand is no longer assumed to be a legal tsumo: the controller checks for an actual yaku and keeps discarding when there is none. Call prompts now prefer the newest board addition over a possibly stale pond tile (the live log claimed 6z/dragon while the actual Pon was 9m), and the log records the last discard tile/seat. {"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.315","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v1.0.4.317 (2026-10-21) [testing]
- **The Cast-Start Stillness setting is removed, together with the v1.0.4.316 testing build it shipped in.** That build held a fresh cast bar for a moment after movement stopped to keep the bar from being glued onto a dodge, but casting into a stop is normal cast mechanics, not a stuck slide-cast, so the hold answered a problem the game does not have. Cast-start movement behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.315 behaviour: moving always blocks a new cast start, instant casts and orbwalker-driven movement never block, and a stopped player casts immediately. The v1.0.4.315 FATE-grind spike skip is untouched. A settings file that still carries the old key loads unchanged; the key is ignored and disappears at the next save.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.316 testing build, which is withdrawn. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.315 (2026-10-20) [testing]
- **The FATE-grind spike skip now stays on.** The first testing build of the part-of-pack spike skip (v1.0.4.314) checked for spiked mobs through its own skip list: with a skip armed, the next check saw the spiked mobs already hidden, believed none were left and switched the skip off, so the spiked mob could be targeted again on alternating ticks. The check now reads the full pack every tick, the skip stays armed while a spiked mob lives, and a pack that decays to only spiked mobs takes the full stop as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.314 testing build. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.314 (2026-10-20) [testing]
- **The enemy-reflect stop no longer freezes a FATE grind over spikes on part of the pack.** While another plugin drives the rotation with FATE priority inside a FATE, a mob carrying a reflect or counter-stance status (Ice Spikes, Shock Spikes, Blaze Spikes, the Counter stances) no longer stops every press for the status's full duration: the rotation attacks the rest of the pack first and leaves the carrier alone. The full stop keeps everything it covered before - manual play, foray territories (Eureka's charged spikes kill), and a pack where every target reflects - and still targets the player and cancels casts there. Every job the grind drives had the same stall, not only Summoner.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.313 (2026-10-20) [testing]
- **Ninja: merged the upstream ninjutsu rework (WrathCombo 95211afb8).** The mudra casts (Fuma Shuriken, Raiton, Katon, Suiton, Huton, Doton, Hyosho Ranryu, Goka Mekkyaku) now track the mudra already pressed as flags and finish the jutsu from that record, replacing the last-action switch; the standalone Fuma Shuriken readiness check is removed, so Fuma is offered whenever the higher jutsu is not yet learned; Hyosho Ranryu and Goka Mekkyaku no longer require Ten to be ready on top of Kassatsu.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.312 (2026-10-19) [testing]
- **White Mage and Astrologian: the timed raidwide AoE regen (Medica II/Medica III, Aspected Helios/Helios Conjunction) now casts once per raidwide.** The scheduled cast that follows the raidwide's damage burst is the only one: while that cast is timed up, the earlier auto-detection no longer fires the same heal as well, and a cast that landed before the burst is not followed by the same regen again while its heal-over-time is still active. After the regen expires, the heal is available as before. Scholar and Sage raidwide shields are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.311 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Deep Dungeon (Palace of the Dead): the sustaining potion is spent inside a behemoth's Ecliptic Meteor window whatever the health slider says.** The floor-180 meteor takes roughly 80% of maximum health, so a potion held back for after the hit is wasted. The gate now treats the meteor window itself as a heal window and rolls the potion in it; the preset toggle, item readiness and the no-Rehabilitation check all still apply, and the health slider keeps ruling everywhere else. A behemoth tracker recognises the two floor-180 behemoths by name and watches the boss's cast and health for the meteor threshold, exposing a hold band (while the cast nears the threshold) and the window (the cast itself) to the job modules below.
- **Ninja: Shade Shift is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor and pressed in the window.** While the behemoth nears its meteor threshold the shield is no longer spent on its own health or incoming-damage triggers; in the window itself it presses even at full health.
- **Summoner: Radiant Aegis banks and presses around the Ecliptic Meteor.** The overcap rule holds the second charge while the behemoth nears the threshold instead of burning it early; the maintain rule keeps a shield up through the window even above its health slider.
- **Black Mage: Manaward is banked for the Ecliptic Meteor in solo play.** The own-health trigger is held while the behemoth nears the threshold; the incoming-damage trigger still presses the ward for the cast itself, so the window stays covered.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.","DalamudApiLevel":15,"Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.

XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.315","Changelog":"v1.0.4.317 (2026-10-21) [testing]

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.315","Changelog":"v1.0.4.320 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is back, now fenced so the cleanse scan can never hang or spin a frame.** Same cleanse behaviour as before the withdrawal: dispellable debuffs are graded by worth (movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer can spare the cast, damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs never take one, doom always, the dead never), hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere, and one debuff can never consume two casts. New in this build, the cleanse scan runs behind a frame guard: it pauses right after a plugin reload and right after any territory change (the two windows the withdrawn build ran into trouble in), can never re-enter itself, and if a single scan ever costs more than a frame the plugin logs the managed call stack at the slow point and stands the scan down for two seconds instead of repeating next tick.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.319 withdrawal build. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.319 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **The v1.0.4.318 automatic-cleanse change is withdrawn; cleanse behaviour is again exactly the v1.0.4.317 behaviour.** The change graded dispellable debuffs by worth, required friendly targets along the Esuna retargeting chain and held a second cleanse back while a first was still resolving, but a full game freeze was reported with the build present, the main thread spinning inside the plugin's own managed code, and the exact looping path could not be established from the captured evidence. The whole change comes out rather than leave a suspected hazard on the heal path: the retargeting chain, the worth checks and the double-cast window of v1.0.4.317 are restored as they were.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Supersedes the v1.0.4.318 testing build, which is withdrawn. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.318 (2026-10-24) [testing]
- **Automatic cleanses (Esuna and Exuviation) now fire only when the debuff is worth the cast, and never twice for the same debuff.** Three defects fixed at one shared verdict. First, the Esuna retargeting chain could resolve a hostile target: a mob carrying its own dispel-flagged damage-over-time effect (for example Combust III on the mob the DoT was cast on) outranked the real party member, so grinding a FATE could spend global cooldowns casting Esuna at a mob. The chain now requires a friendly target at every step, and hostile objects can no longer resolve as cleanse candidates anywhere. Second, the heal-combo cleanse branch and the auto-rotation's party cleanse were two independent casters for the same debuff while the status list still showed a debuff that a cast already in flight was removing, so one debuff could consume two casts seconds apart. Every cleanse send now goes through one shared verdict that remembers a cleanse sent in the last few seconds and stands down until it resolves. Third, every dispellable status was treated as equally worth a cast. The verdict now grades them: movement- and action-locking debuffs cleanse first, because cleansing them is the dodge; damage-over-time debuffs cleanse while the healer is healthy enough to spare the cast; damage-taken amplifiers and resist downs that fall off on their own never take one. Under low health only a cleansing doom is still worth the cast, and a dead candidate is never targeted.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.317 (2026-10-21) [testing]
- **The Cast-Start Stillness setting is removed, together with the v1.0.4.316 testing build it shipped in.** That build held a fresh cast bar for a moment after movement stopped to keep the bar from being glued onto a dodge, but casting into a stop is normal cast mechanics, not a stuck slide-cast, so the hold answered a problem the game does not have. {"Author":"DhogGPT","Name":"Deep Ducking","Punchline":"Deep Ducking public host and authenticated module access.","Description":"The Deep Ducking public host provides the introduction, community links and authenticated loading of separately supplied DDuck modules. /deepducking and /dduck open the introduction when no module is loaded.

/deepducking [toggle main window]
/dduck [alias for /deepducking; accepts all commands below]
/deepducking mini [toggle Mini]
/deepducking settings [open Settings]
/deepducking config [open Settings]
/deepducking debug [reveal and open Advanced for this plugin load]
/deepducking help [open command help]
/deepducking start [floor] [start or continue selected save; optional fresh-run floor]
/deepducking party-start [floor] [alias for start]
/deepducking party [select fixed-party POTD while idle]
/deepducking adopt [bind eligible already-entered party dungeon]
/deepducking hold [pause local output; retain run for Resume]
/deepducking resume [resume retained local run after readiness checks]
/deepducking nextstop [exit after next boss]
/deepducking ns [exit after next boss]
/deepducking stop [FULL STOP; persist local lock across reloads; stay in duty]
/deepducking reset-stop [clear eligible FULL STOP after cleanup; do not start]
/deepducking status [print local status]
/deepducking inspect [record read-only client and native observations]
/deepducking saves [open Saves]
/deepducking saves info <dungeon> [inspect native saves]
/deepducking saves delete <dungeon> <1|2> [delete selected save after native checks; no extra confirmation]
/deepducking saves dof <dungeon> <1|2> <on|off> [set future-failure deletion preference; no deletion now]
/deepducking saves cancel [cancel pending save or Start preparation; completed actions remain]

Dungeon arguments: potd, hoh, eo, pt. [floor] is optional; <...> is required. Choose one value for 1|2 or on|off; omit brackets when typing. Start can replace stopped state; Resume can release an eligible retained in-dungeon run. nextstop and ns retain the save and keep Mini open until return is observed; repeat to confirm the same request.
